mainTopic: The special laws of the כהן גדול and similar כהנים, how a כהן גדול mourns, and the rules of what comes first
overview: The גמרא shows that the second half of the משנה, about a former כהן גדול, follows רבי מאיר. That raises a problem: the first half follows the רבנן, who argue with him. רב חסדא, רב יוסף and רבא each answer this. רבא says the whole משנה is רבי שמעון, and a ברייתא listing the special laws of a כהן גדול backs him up. The גמרא then shows which of these laws also apply to the משוח מלחמה, using פסוקים in ויקרא 21. A question about a כהן גדול with צרעת marrying an אלמנה is answered from a ברייתא about a כהן גדול with מומין. A new משנה teaches how a כהן גדול tears his clothes in mourning, and that he may serve as an אונן. רב and שמואל argue about where he tears. A last משנה teaches that whatever is more frequent, and whoever is holier, comes first, and the גמרא finds a source for each rule.

steps.title: Quoting the second half of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the סיפא: the only differences between a serving כהן גדול and a former one are the פר of יום הכיפורים and the עשירית האיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now look at the second part of the משנה: the only difference between a כהן גדול who is serving now and one who used to serve is the bull of יום הכיפורים and the tenth-of-an-ephah offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next line of the משנה so it can figure out whose opinion it follows. This is a setup for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the former כהן גדול is the same as the serving one in every way except two. That means he still has the status of a כהן גדול for almost everything. This detail is what will link the line to רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause or second part of a משנה
The כהן גדול who is serving right now
A כהן גדול who stepped aside and is no longer serving
The bull the כהן גדול brings on יום הכיפורים
The daily flour offering of a tenth of an ephah brought by the כהן גדול

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין כֹּהֵן מְשַׁמֵּשׁ לְכֹהֵן שֶׁעָבַר
phrases.english: There is no difference between a serving High Priest and a former High Priest
phrases.notes: Both kinds of כהן here are a כהן גדול, even though the word גדול isn't written.

phrases.english: except the bull of Yom Kippur
and the tenth of an ephah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier analysis of the רישא by now turning to the סיפא of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A former כהן גדול differs from a serving one only in the פר of יום הכיפורים and the עשירית האיפה.

steps.title: The second half matches רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the סיפא follows רבי מאיר. It brings a ברייתא where רבי מאיר rules that the replacement כהן גדול still carries all the מצוות of a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we have reached רבי מאיר's opinion. A ברייתא teaches: if a כהן גדול became disqualified and stepped aside, and they appointed another כהן in his place, the first goes back to his job. The second still has all the מצוות of a כהן גדול on him. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the author of the סיפא as רבי מאיר and proves it from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי מאיר's view, the replacement who steps down keeps the full status of a כהן גדול. That is exactly what the משנה implies when it says a former כהן גדול differs in only two things. So the סיפא fits רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: We have arrived at; this part follows the opinion of...
A disqualification, such as becoming temporarily unable to serve
The מצוות and rules that apply to a כהן גדול

phrases.english: We have arrived at Rabbi Meir.
As it is taught in a baraita:
If a disqualification happened to a High Priest
and he stepped aside, and they appointed another priest in his place,
the first returns to his service,
and the second, all the מצוות of the High Priesthood are upon him,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the סיפא quoted in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the סיפא of the משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי מאיר rules that the replacement כהן גדול keeps all the מצוות of a כהן גדול.

steps.title: רבי יוסי disagrees and tells a story
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rules that the replacement cannot serve as a כהן גדול or as a כהן הדיוט. He backs this up with the story of יוסף בן אילים of צפורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: the first goes back to his job, and the second is not fit to be a כהן גדול or a regular כהן. רבי יוסי said: there was a case with יוסף בן אילים from צפורי. A כהן גדול became disqualified and stepped aside, and they appointed יוסף בן אילים in his place. Afterward, his fellow כהנים did not let him serve as a כהן גדול or as a regular כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the opposing view of רבי יוסי, supported by a real event.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says the replacement stays a full כהן גדול. רבי יוסי says the replacement cannot serve in either role. The story shows that the כהנים actually acted this way, and this disagreement is why the סיפא can only match רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary כהן, not the כהן גדול
An incident or real-life case brought as support
They did not allow him
His fellow כהנים

steps.confusionAlert: יוסף בן אילים was the replacement, not the כהן גדול who became disqualified. He is the 'second' כהן in רבי יוסי's ruling.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
phrases.notes: The square brackets mark the corrected wording; some versions don't have רבי יוסי's ruling here at all.

phrases.english: the first returns to his service,
and the second is not fit

phrases.aramaic: לֹא לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל וְלֹא לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט].
phrases.english: neither as a High Priest nor as an ordinary priest.
Rabbi Yosei said:
There was an incident with Yosef ben Eilim of Tzippori
where a disqualification happened to the High Priest,
and he stepped aside, and they appointed another in his place,
and his brethren the priests did not allow him

phrases.aramaic: לִהְיוֹת לֹא כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וְלֹא כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט.
phrases.english: to be neither a High Priest nor an ordinary priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing side of the ברייתא quoted in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, the replacement כהן גדול may serve neither as a כהן גדול nor as a כהן הדיוט.

steps.title: Why the replacement could not serve in either role
steps.stepSummary: He cannot be a כהן גדול because of ill will, and he cannot be a כהן הדיוט because we raise people up in holiness and never bring them down.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could not be a כהן גדול because it would cause bad feelings. He could not be a regular כהן because in holy matters we move people up and never down.
steps.whatsHappening: The text explains the two reasons behind the כהנים' decision in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having two equal כהנים גדולים would create jealousy and resentment, so the replacement cannot stay a כהן גדול. Sending him back to being an ordinary כהן would be a demotion in holiness, which is not done. So he is left unable to serve in either role.

keyTerms.meaning: Ill will, resentment, or jealousy
In holy matters we raise up and do not bring down

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule מעלין בקודש ואין מורידין is a well-known principle that appears in many places in הלכה.

phrases.english: Not a High Priest, because of ill will;
not an ordinary priest
because one raises up in holiness and does not bring down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons behind רבי יוסי's ruling and the story in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The replacement cannot be a כהן גדול because of איבה, and cannot be a כהן הדיוט because מעלין בקודש ואין מורידין.

steps.title: Can one משנה follow two opposing views?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether it makes sense that the רישא follows the רבנן while the סיפא follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really possible that the first part follows the רבנן and the second part follows רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem: the two halves of the same משנה seem to follow two sides of one argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא showed that the רישא follows the רבנן, who argue with רבי מאיר. Now the סיפא follows רבי מאיר. It is strange for one משנה to switch between opposing opinions in the middle.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause or opening part of a משנה
The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with an individual תנא

phrases.english: The first clause is the Rabbis and the latter clause is Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result of step 2 in light of the earlier finding about the רישא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the סיפא follows רבי מאיר while the רישא follows the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single משנה should not split between two opposing sides of the same dispute.

steps.title: רב חסדא: Yes, it really is split
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא accepts the difficulty: the רישא follows the רבנן and the סיפא follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Yes, the first part is the רבנן and the second part is רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers by simply agreeing that the משנה is split between two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא does not try to find a single author. He accepts that the two halves of the משנה follow different תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes; indeed

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: אִין, רֵישָׁא רַבָּנַן וְסֵיפָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: Yes, the first clause is the Rabbis and the latter clause is Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 by accepting it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the split: the משנה really does follow two different תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A single משנה must have one author.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא follows the רבנן and the סיפא follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רב יוסף: רבי arranged it using different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the whole משנה is רבי, who chose to teach each part according to a different תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: it is רבי, and he taught it following different תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a different answer: one editor, רבי, wrote the whole משנה but deliberately picked a different opinion for each part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף agrees that each half matches a different תנא. But he explains it as one deliberate choice by רבי, who arranged the משנה. On the extra-garments כהן he followed the רבנן, and on the former כהן גדול he followed רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught it according to different תנאים

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is Rebbi,
and he formulated it according to different Tannaim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the קשיא of step 5, different from רב חסדא's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Single editor who chose different opinions for each part.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The split means the משנה has no single author.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי wrote it all, selecting the opinion he preferred for each case.

steps.title: רבא: It is all רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the whole משנה is רבי שמעון, who agrees with רבי מאיר on one issue and disagrees with him on the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it is רבי שמעון. He holds like רבי מאיר on one point and argues with him on the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third answer: the whole משנה follows one תנא, רבי שמעון, whose opinion happens to match each part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא finds one תנא who holds both halves of the משנה at once. רבי שמעון agrees with רבי מאיר that a former כהן גדול keeps his status, which matches the סיפא. He disagrees with רבי מאיר about the כהן appointed by extra garments, which matches the רישא, so there is no real split.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like...
In one matter
He disagrees with him

steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers to how the רישא follows the רבנן and the סיפא follows רבי מאיר. רב חסדא: it really is split. רב יוסף: רבי arranged it using different תנאים. רבא: it is all רבי שמעון, who agrees with רבי מאיר on one issue and disagrees on the other.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is Rabbi Shimon,
and he holds like Rabbi Meir in one matter,
phrases.notes: This is the former כהן גדול, the case in the סיפא.

phrases.english: and disagrees with him in one matter.
phrases.notes: This is the כהן appointed by wearing the extra garments, the case in the רישא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third answer to the קשיא of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a single תנא whose combined view matches both halves.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two halves must come from opposing sides of the רבי מאיר and רבנן dispute.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון holds both halves: he agrees with רבי מאיר on the former כהן גדול and disagrees with him on the extra-garments כהן.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists how a כהן גדול differs from a regular כהן
steps.stepSummary: To support רבא, the גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It begins listing the special laws of a כהן גדול: his special offerings, his mourning rules, his marriage rules, and his role in freeing the accidental killer.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: These are the differences between a כהן גדול and a regular כהן. He brings the bull for any of the מצוות, the bull of יום הכפורים, and the tenth of an איפה. He may not let his hair grow long or tear his clothes in mourning. If he does tear, he tears from below, while a regular כהן tears from above. He may not become impure for a dead relative. He is commanded to marry a virgin, and he may not marry a widow. His death lets the accidental killer go home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רבא's claim that the whole משנה is רבי שמעון. This step starts the ברייתא's list of things that make a כהן גדול different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list itself is not the proof yet. The גמרא sets out the full list first. Later the ברייתא will say which items apply to a מרובה בגדים and which apply to a משיח שעבר, and that is where the proof comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
The bull a כהן גדול brings for a mistaken ruling about any מצוה
The daily flour offering of the כהן גדול (a tenth of an איפה)
Letting the hair grow long and tearing the clothes, which are signs of mourning
His death lets the accidental killer leave the עיר מקלט and go home

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: The matters that are between

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט אֵלּוּ הֵם:
phrases.english: a כהן גדול and a regular כהן are these:
the bull that comes for any of the מצוות,
and the bull of יום הכפורים, and the tenth of an איפה,
and he does not let his hair grow long, and he does not tear his clothes.
But he tears from below,
and the regular כהן tears from above.
And he does not become impure for relatives,
and he is commanded to marry a virgin, and he is forbidden to a widow,
and he brings back the killer,
phrases.notes: This means the accidental killer, who can go home from the עיר מקלט when the כהן גדול dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבא's answer in Step 8
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that one תנא (רבי שמעון) holds the רבנן's view on מרובה בגדים and רבי מאיר's view on משיח שעבר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the differences between a כהן גדול and a כהן הדיוט

steps.title: More special laws of the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on with the list. A כהן גדול can serve as an אונן, takes first choice of service and portions, wears eight garments, alone does the יום הכפורים service, and is exempt from the offering for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may bring offerings as an אונן, but he does not eat from them and does not take a share of them. He offers whatever part he wants first, and he takes whatever portion he wants first. He serves in eight garments. The whole יום הכפורים service is valid only if he does it. He is exempt from bringing an offering for entering the מקדש while impure or eating קדשים while impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list of the special laws of a כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pay attention to the last item, that he is exempt from the offering for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. Later in this daf (Steps 13–14), רב פפא will use this exact item to prove the ברייתא is רבי שמעון's.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the day a close relative dies
Having first choice of which service to do and which portion to take
The eight special garments of the כהן גדול
Entering the מקדש or eating קדשים while impure

phrases.english: And he offers sacrifices as an אונן,
but he does not eat, and he does not take a share.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: He offers a part first,
and he takes a portion first,
and he serves in eight garments.
And all the service of יום הכפורים
is valid only when done by him,
and he is exempt for impurity of the מקדש and its holy foods.
phrases.notes: He means he is exempt from the special offering that others bring for this sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the whole משנה is רבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rest of the ברייתא's list, including the exemption from טומאת מקדש וקדשיו

steps.title: Which laws apply to a מרובה בגדים and to a former כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says all these laws apply to a מרובה בגדים except the bull for all the מצוות. It says all of them apply to a משיח שעבר except the bull of יום הכפורים and the tenth of an איפה. This is the same mix of views that רבא described.
steps.simpleTranslation: All these laws apply to a כהן גדול appointed by wearing the extra garments, except the bull brought for all the מצוות. All these laws apply to a former anointed כהן גדול, except the bull of יום הכפורים and the tenth of an איפה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the proof. The ברייתא says which laws apply to two kinds of כהן גדול, and its answers match רבא's mix of opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the מרובה בגדים, the ברייתא says he does not bring the פר for all the מצוות. That matches the רבנן. On the משיח שעבר, it says he does bring that פר and is missing only the יום הכפורים offerings. That matches רבי מאיר. So one ברייתא really does hold the רבנן's view on one question and רבי מאיר's view on the other, just as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן גדול appointed by wearing the extra garments, without being anointed with oil
A former anointed כהן גדול who has stepped down
Except for

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא puts the מרובה בגדים with the רבנן (no פר for all the מצוות) and the משיח שעבר with רבי מאיר (he does bring it). That is exactly רבא's split.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two exceptions. The מרובה בגדים is missing only the פר for all the מצוות. The משיח שעבר is missing only the יום הכפורים bull and the daily flour offering.

phrases.english: And all of them apply to the one with extra garments,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִפַּר הַמֵּבִיא עַל כׇּל הַמִּצְוֹת,
phrases.english: except for the bull brought for all the מצוות,
and all of them apply to an anointed one who has stepped down,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִפַּר יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים וַעֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה,
phrases.english: except for the bull of יום הכפורים and the tenth of an איפה,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא's list to the two kinds of כהן גדול discussed in רבא's answer
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that one תנא agrees with רבי מאיר on משיח שעבר and with the רבנן on מרובה בגדים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's rules for מרובה בגדים and משיח שעבר

steps.title: The war-anointed כהן and the argument over the accidental killer
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that none of these laws apply to the משוח מלחמה except five listed in the פרשה. רבי יהודה counts freeing the accidental killer among them, and the חכמים disagree on that point.
steps.simpleTranslation: None of these laws apply to the כהן anointed for war, except five things said in the פרשה: he does not let his hair grow long or tear his clothes, he does not become impure for relatives, he is commanded to marry a virgin, he is forbidden to marry a widow, and his death frees the accidental killer. These are the words of רבי יהודה. The חכמים say: his death does not free the killer.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with one more kind of כהן, the משוח מלחמה. It lists the few laws that apply to him and records a disagreement about one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This last section is not part of the proof for רבא. The גמרא quotes it because it is how the ברייתא ends. רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue only about whether the death of the משוח מלחמה frees the accidental killer.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן anointed to speak to and go out with the army
The things said in the Torah section about the כהן גדול
The Sages, the majority view

phrases.english: and none of them apply to the one anointed for war,
except for five things stated in the section:
phrases.notes: This means the Torah section about the כהן גדול, ויקרא 21.

phrases.english: he does not let his hair grow long and does not tear his clothes,
and he does not become impure for relatives,
and he is commanded to marry a virgin, and he is forbidden to a widow,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַחֲזִיר אֶת הָרוֹצֵחַ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: and he brings back the killer; these are the words of רבי יהודה.
And the חכמים say: He does not bring him back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with the case of the משוח מלחמה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only five of the כהן גדול's laws apply to the משוח מלחמה. רבי יהודה and the חכמים disagree about whether his death frees the accidental killer.

steps.title: How do we know this ברייתא is רבי שמעון's?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what shows that this ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this ברייתא, from where do we know that it is רבי שמעון's?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא never says whose opinion it is, so the גמרא asks how we know it belongs to רבי שמעון. This question sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only helps רבא if it is רבי שמעון's. Otherwise it would just show that some unnamed תנא holds this mix of views. So the גמרא needs a clear sign in the ברייתא that points to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (do we know)?

phrases.english: And this one, from where do we know
that it is רבי שמעון's?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the link between the ברייתא and רבי שמעון
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What in the ברייתא shows that its author is רבי שמעון

steps.title: רב פפא: Only רבי שמעון exempts the כהן גדול for טומאת מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא points to the ruling that the כהן גדול is exempt from the offering for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. Only רבי שמעון holds that view, so the ברייתא must be his.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Who have you heard say that the כהן גדול is exempt for impurity of the מקדש and its holy foods? רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. He points to one ruling in the ברייתא that only רבי שמעון holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in Step 10, the ברייתא said the כהן גדול is exempt from the offering for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. That is known to be רבי שמעון's own view. So the whole ברייתא is his, and it shows that רבי שמעון agrees with רבי מאיר on משיח שעבר and with the רבנן on מרובה בגדים. This supports רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Who have you heard who says...? This means only one known opinion holds this view.
The offering whose cost depends on the person's wealth, brought for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו

steps.whatToRemember: A ruling that only one תנא holds works like a fingerprint. Because the ברייתא exempts the כהן גדול from the offering for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, it must be רבי שמעון's. That backs up רבא's answer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common method in the גמרא. When one ruling in a source belongs to a known תנא, the whole source is credited to him.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
Whom have you heard who says,
"exempt for impurity of the מקדש and its holy foods"?
phrases.notes: This points back to the ruling in Step 10.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא exempts the כהן גדול from the offering for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, which is רבי שמעון's own view. So the ברייתא is his, and that supports רבא.

steps.title: Where do the five shared laws come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the end of the ברייתא about the five laws of the משוח מלחמה and asks for their source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said the משוח מלחמה has none of these laws except the five stated in the פרשה. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up the last line of the ברייתא and asks for its source in the תורה. This sets up the next step, where a second ברייתא gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא simply stated that five laws of the כהן גדול also apply to the משוח מלחמה. Now the גמרא wants to see which פסוקים teach this.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן anointed to lead the people into war
A section of the תורה; here, the laws of the כהן גדול in ויקרא 21
From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: Except for five matters
phrases.notes: This is the last line of the ברייתא from step 12, about the משוח מלחמה.

phrases.english: that are stated in the portion.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's final clause from step 12 and asks for its scriptural source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches which כהן גדול laws also apply to the משוח מלחמה.

steps.title: One פסוק describes three kinds of כהנים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads ויקרא 21:10 as speaking about three kinds of כהנים. It applies the laws of hair, garments and the dead to all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'The כהן who is greater than his brothers' means the כהן גדול. 'On whose head the anointing oil is poured' means the משוח מלחמה. 'Who is consecrated to wear the garments' means the מרובה בגדים. About all of them the פסוק says: he may not let his hair grow wild, may not tear his clothes, and may not come near any dead body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that splits one פסוק into three phrases. Each phrase stands for a different kind of high כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since all three kinds of כהנים appear in the same פסוק, the next laws in that פסוק apply to all of them. That gives us the first three of the five shared laws: hair, tearing clothes, and contact with the dead.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן גדול who was made כהן גדול by wearing the eight garments, not by anointing oil
The anointing oil
He may not let his hair grow long (as a mourner does)
He may not tear his clothes (as a mourner does)

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"And the priest who is greater than his brothers"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:10

phrases.english: this is the High Priest,
"upon whose head the anointing oil is poured"
this is the priest anointed for war,
"and who is consecrated to wear the garments"
this is the one consecrated by the extra garments.
About all of them it says:
"He shall not let his hair grow wild, nor tear his garments,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל כׇּל נַפְשֹׁת מֵת לֹא יָבֹא״.
phrases.english: nor come near any dead body."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק names all three kinds of כהנים together, so the rules of hair, garments and the dead apply to all three.

steps.title: The משוח מלחמה may not serve as an אונן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules out the idea that all three may bring קרבנות as an אונן. The word עליו limits this to the כהן גדול himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think all of them may bring קרבנות while they are an אונן. So the פסוק says: 'for the crown of his God's anointing oil is upon him.' Upon him, and not upon the other one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: maybe all three kinds of כהנים may serve as an אונן. It then uses a word in the פסוק to show that they may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, all three shared every law in the פסוק. The word עליו ('upon him') narrows the next law, serving as an אונן, so that it does not include the משוח מלחמה. This is the point where the תורה separates the משוח מלחמה from the כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the day a close relative died, before the burial
You might have thought (introduces a wrong idea that the פסוק corrects)
Therefore the פסוק says
Upon him; a limiting word

phrases.english: One might think all of them may sacrifice as acute mourners?
Therefore the verse states:
"For the crown of his God's anointing oil is upon him"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:12

phrases.english: "Upon him," and not upon his fellow.
phrases.notes: He means the כהן גדול, and not the כהן anointed for war.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and limits one law to the כהן גדול alone.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that only the כהן גדול may serve as an אונן.

steps.title: The word והוא brings the משוח מלחמה back for בתולה
steps.stepSummary: After the תורה separated the משוח מלחמה, one might think he is not commanded to marry a בתולה. The word והוא includes him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that the פסוק separated them, you might think the משוח מלחמה is not commanded to marry a בתולה. So the פסוק says 'And he.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא worries that once the משוח מלחמה was left out of one law, he is left out of all the laws after it. It uses the extra letter ו in והוא to bring him back in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 removed the משוח מלחמה from the law of אונן. Without a new source, he might be dropped from the next law too. The ו ('and') joins him back in for the law of marrying a בתולה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who was never married; the כהן גדול must marry one
'And he'; the extra ו includes someone
The פסוק separated him

phrases.english: And after the verse separated him,

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהֵא מְצֻוֶּוה עַל הַבְּתוּלָה?
phrases.english: one might think he is not commanded regarding a virgin?
Therefore the verse states: "And he."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:13. The extra 'and' brings the משוח מלחמה back in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 17 excluded the משוח מלחמה from one law, this step includes him again in the next law.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the משוח מלחמה must marry a בתולה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ו of והוא in ויקרא 21:13.

steps.title: This matches רבי ישמעאל's reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this ברייתא follows a תנאים dispute. רבי ישמעאל reads והוא as including the משוח מלחמה after the פסוק separated him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of תנאים. 'And he shall take a wife in her virginity': after the פסוק separated him, it included him again. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the reading of והוא we just saw is really one side of a dispute between תנאים. Here it gives רבי ישמעאל's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל uses והוא just as our ברייתא did, to include the משוח מלחמה in the law of בתולה. So our ברייתא fits his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute between תנאים
It included (added someone to the law)

phrases.english: This is parallel to a dispute of tanna'im:
"And he shall take a wife in her virginity,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:13

phrases.english: after the verse separated him, it included him.
These are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the ברייתא's reading of והוא to רבי ישמעאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, והוא includes the משוח מלחמה in the law of marrying a בתולה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא uses והוא for a different case
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא uses the word והוא to include a כהן גדול who stepped down because of מומין, not the משוח מלחמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: I only know that a כהן גדול who stepped down because of a seminal emission must marry a בתולה. From where do I know this about one who stepped down because of blemishes? So the פסוק says 'And he.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the other side of the dispute. רבי עקיבא uses the same word והוא to teach something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, והוא teaches that a כהן גדול who stopped serving because of a lasting blemish must still marry a בתולה. Since he uses the word for this, there is no extra word left to include the משוח מלחמה.

keyTerms.meaning: A seminal emission; it makes a כהן unfit to serve for a short time
Physical blemishes that make a כהן unfit to serve for good
Who stepped down from his post

steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא use the same word והוא. They do not argue about the word itself. They argue about whom it comes to include.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁעָבַר מֵחֲמַת קִרְיוֹ,
phrases.english: I have only one who stepped down because of his seminal emission,
from where do I know one who stepped down because of blemishes?
Therefore the verse states: "And he."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁעָבַר מֵחֲמַת קִרְיוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing תנא view to רבי ישמעאל's reading of והוא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, והוא includes a כהן גדול who stepped down because of blemishes in the law of marrying a בתולה.

steps.title: רבא asks about a כהן גדול who became a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן whether a כהן גדול who got צרעת may marry an אלמנה. Is he only pushed aside, or fully released from his status?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: an anointed כהן גדול who became a מצורע, what is the law about marrying a widow? Is he just pushed aside, or is he released completely?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new question about a כהן גדול with צרעת. He asks whether he is still bound by the ban on marrying an אלמנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to see it. If he is only pushed aside for now, he is still a כהן גדול and may not marry an אלמנה. If he is released from his position, he becomes like a regular כהן and may marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him
Became afflicted with צרעת
A widow; a כהן גדול may not marry one
He is only pushed aside (for now)
He is fully released (from his status)

steps.whyThisMatters: The question tests whether a lasting problem that stops a כהן גדול from serving also takes away his special status and its rules.

phrases.english: Rava asked of Rav Nachman:
An anointed High Priest who became leprous,
what is the law regarding a widow?
Is he just pushed aside,
or is he fully released?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a כהן גדול who stepped down because of מומין to one who stepped down because of צרעת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a כהן גדול with צרעת keeps his status, and so may not marry an אלמנה, or loses it.

steps.title: רב נחמן had no answer
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן did not have an answer at that time. The next step brings a ברייתא that answers it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not have the answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that רב נחמן did not know the answer to רבא's question. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At this point רב נחמן had no source to settle the question. The next step brings a ברייתא showing that a כהן גדול who stepped down because of מומין keeps his status. That settles the case of צרעת.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not in his hand; he did not have an answer

steps.whatToRemember: The משוח מלחמה shares the laws of hair, tearing clothes, the dead, and marrying a בתולה (according to רבי ישמעאל), but he may not serve as an אונן. רבא's question about a כהן גדול with צרעת is answered in the next step.

phrases.english: It was not available to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports that רב נחמן could not answer רבא's question. Step 23 supplies the answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן could not answer. The answer comes in the next step from a ברייתא.

steps.title: A ברייתא answers the question about the כהן גדול with צרעת
steps.stepSummary: הונא בריה דרב נחמן quotes a ברייתא: a כהן גדול who stepped down because of מומין is included by the word והוא, so he still must marry a בתולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another time רב פפא was sitting and asking the same question. הונא son of רב נחמן told him: We learned in a ברייתא: I would only know this about a כהן גדול who stepped down because of קרי. How do I know it about one who stepped down because of מומין? The פסוק says "and he."
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises the same question that רב נחמן could not answer, and הונא בריה דרב נחמן answers it with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the מצוה to marry a בתולה stays even on a כהן גדול who stepped down because of מומין. צרעת is a kind of מום, so a כהן גדול with צרעת still has his full status and may not marry an אלמנה. This is the same reading of והוא that רבי עקיבא gave in step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: Once / on another occasion
A seminal emission, which makes a כהן temporarily unfit to serve
Physical blemishes that disqualify a כהן from serving
The פסוק teaches

steps.whyThisMatters: It answers the question רב נחמן could not answer in step 22. A כהן גדול who is pushed aside by a lasting blemish has not lost his special marriage rules.

phrases.english: Once Rav Pappa was sitting
and he was asking this question
phrases.notes: This is the same question רבא asked רב נחמן in step 21, about a כהן גדול with צרעת marrying an אלמנה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן לְרַב פָּפָּא
phrases.english: Huna son of Rav Nachman said to Rav Pappa

phrases.aramaic: תְּנֵינָא: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁעָבַר מֵחֲמַת קִרְיוֹ
phrases.english: We learned: I only know about one who stepped down because of his seminal emission
From where do we know it about one who stepped down because of blemishes?
The verse says: "And he"

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה הונא בריה דרב נחמן לרב פפא תנינא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question that רב נחמן could not answer in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a כהן גדול with צרעת is only pushed aside or fully released from his status.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא includes a כהן גדול who stepped down because of מומין in the מצוה to marry a בתולה, so his status remains and he may not marry an אלמנה.

steps.title: רב פפא honors הונא for his answer
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא kisses הונא on the head and gives him his daughter to marry.
steps.simpleTranslation: He got up, kissed him on his head, and gave him his daughter as a wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רב פפא showing how much he valued the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the הלכה here. The strong reaction shows that the answer settled a question that even רב נחמן could not answer, so the question is now closed.

keyTerms.meaning: He kissed him
His daughter

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן גדול who has צרעת, or any lasting מום, still keeps his status: he must marry a בתולה and may not marry an אלמנה.

phrases.english: He got up and kissed him on his head
and gave him his daughter
phrases.notes: Meaning as a wife for הונא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by showing that the answer in step 23 was accepted.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question is resolved: a כהן גדול with צרעת may not marry an אלמנה.

steps.title: משנה: How a כהן גדול tears his garments in mourning
steps.stepSummary: A כהן גדול tears his clothing from below, while a regular כהן tears from above.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A כהן גדול tears his garments from below, and an ordinary כהן tears from above.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a כהן גדול tears his clothes for a dead relative differently from a regular כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says a כהן גדול may not tear his garments the usual way. The משנה says he still tears, but from below. It does not explain exactly where "below" and "above" are; the גמרא will argue about that next.

keyTerms.meaning: Tears (his garment, as a sign of mourning)
An ordinary כהן, not the כהן גדול
From below
From above

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A High Priest tears from below
and the ordinary priest from above

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new subject.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול tears his garments from below; an ordinary כהן tears from above.

steps.title: משנה: A כהן גדול may serve as an אונן but not eat
steps.stepSummary: On the day a close relative dies, a כהן גדול may bring קרבנות but not eat from them. A regular כהן may do neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן גדול may offer קרבנות while he is an אונן, but he may not eat from them. An ordinary כהן neither offers nor eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second difference between a כהן גדול and a regular כהן in mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually an אונן is not allowed to do the עבודה. The כהן גדול is an exception and may offer קרבנות, but even he may not eat from them.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the day his close relative died
Offers a קרבן
Eats (from the קרבנות)

phrases.english: A High Priest offers sacrifices while he is an acute mourner
but does not eat
and the ordinary priest neither offers nor eats

steps.triggerLanguage: כהן גדול מקריב אונן ולא אוכל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second rule in the same משנה about how a כהן גדול mourns.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול who is an אונן may offer קרבנות but not eat them; an ordinary כהן who is an אונן may do neither.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about where the tear is made
steps.stepSummary: רב says below and above mean the bottom and top of the garment. שמואל says both tear at the neck, just below or at the neckline.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב said: "Below" means really below, and "above" means really above. שמואל said: "Below" means below the neckline, and "above" means at the neckline itself. Both tear at the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the words "below" and "above" in the משנה, and רב and שמואל disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the כהן גדול tears at the bottom of his garment, far from the usual place. For שמואל, both tear at the neck: the regular כהן tears through the neckline, while the כהן גדול tears just under it and leaves the neckline whole.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, literally
The edge or hem of the garment at the neckline
Neck

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix them up: in שמואל's view both tears are at the neck. The only difference is whether the neckline edge itself is torn.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav said
"Below" means really below
"Above" means really above
And Shmuel said
"Below" means below the neckline edge
"Above" means above the neckline edge
phrases.notes: He means the neckline edge itself gets torn.

phrases.english: and both this one and that one tear at the neck

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words "below" and "above" from the משנה in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the bottom of the garment versus the top. שמואל: both at the neck, below the neckline edge versus the edge itself.

steps.title: A ברייתא about tearing the neckline challenges שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that a tear at the neck counts as a real tear even if the neckline edge is not torn through, so a כהן גדול tearing there would break the rule of לא יפרם.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: For all other dead relatives, if he wants he tears through his neckline edge, and if he wants he does not. For his father and mother he must tear through it. Since a tear like that normally counts as a tear, we can apply here the פסוק "he shall not tear his garments"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's view using a ברייתא about the usual laws of tearing for a dead relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that for most relatives, a tear at the neck that leaves the neckline edge whole still counts as a proper mourning tear. So the tear שמואל gives the כהן גדול is a real mourning tear, which the תורה forbids him to make. This supports רב, who sends the כהן גדול to the bottom of the garment.

keyTerms.meaning: Tears through and separates (the neckline edge)
Apply here (the פסוק)
In general, in ordinary cases

phrases.english: They objected: For all the other dead
if he wants, he tears through his neckline edge

phrases.aramaic: רָצָה אֵינוֹ מַבְדִּיל קַמֵּי שָׂפָה שֶׁלּוֹ
phrases.english: if he wants, he does not tear through his neckline edge
for his father and his mother, he must tear through it
Since in general this counts as a tear
phrases.notes: He means a tear at the neck that leaves the edge whole, which is exactly what שמואל gives the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: apply here: "He shall not tear his garments"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's opinion from step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that the כהן גדול tears at the neck, just below the neckline edge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A neck tear without tearing the edge counts as a real tear in ordinary mourning, so a כהן גדול making it would break the rule of "he shall not tear his garments."

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי יהודה on what counts as a real tear
steps.stepSummary: שמואל holds like רבי יהודה, who says a tear that does not split the garment's edge is only a pointless tear, not a real קריעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל agrees with רבי יהודה, who said: any tear that does not split the garment's edge is only a meaningless tear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 28. A tear near the neck that leaves the edge whole does not count as a real tear, so a כהן גדול may tear there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 28 counted a neck tear as real even if the edge stayed whole. שמואל simply follows a different תנא, רבי יהודה, who says that kind of tear is not a real tear. So the כהן גדול who tears just below the neckline is not breaking לא יפרם.

keyTerms.meaning: the edge or hem of the garment, here the neckline
splits apart, separates
a pointless or meaningless tear that does not count as mourning tearing
he holds, he agrees with

phrases.english: Shmuel holds like Rabbi Yehuda
who said: any tear
that does not split apart its edge
is nothing but a pointless tear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 28 by tying שמואל to רבי יהודה's definition of a real tear.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the view to a תנא who disagrees with the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A tear at the neck counts as a real tear even if the edge stays whole, so the כהן גדול would be breaking לא יפרם.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יהודה, such a tear is only a pointless tear, so the כהן גדול may tear there.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה even allow a כהן גדול to tear?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה holds a כהן גדול does not tear his clothes at all, so how can שמואל rely on him for a ruling about how the כהן גדול tears?
steps.simpleTranslation: But does רבי יהודה hold that a כהן גדול tears at all? A ברייתא teaches: if the פסוק had said 'a head he shall not let grow wild and a garment he shall not tear,' I might think it speaks about the head and garment of a סוטה. So it says 'his head' and 'his garments,' teaching that the כהן גדול does not grow his hair or tear at all. That is רבי יהודה's view. רבי ישמעאל says he does not tear the normal way. Instead he tears from below and a regular כהן tears from above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 29. It brings a ברייתא showing that רבי יהודה says a כהן גדול never tears in mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says the כהן גדול does tear, just at the neck. But רבי יהודה reads 'his garments he shall not tear' as a full ban on tearing for a כהן גדול. So it seems שמואל cannot be following רבי יהודה. The view that the כהן גדול tears from below belongs to רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: letting the hair grow wild, a sign of mourning
tearing the garment
a woman suspected by her husband of being unfaithful
at all
a regular כהן, not the כהן גדול

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה does not say the כהן גדול tears 'from below.' That is רבי ישמעאל. רבי יהודה says he does not tear at all.

But it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says:
"His head he shall not let grow wild
and his garments he shall not tear"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:10

phrases.english: that he is not part of growing hair and tearing at all
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yishmael says: he does not tear
the way people usually tear
Rather, he tears from below
and the regular kohen tears from above.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קְרִיעָה בְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 29's claim that שמואל follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that שמואל follows רבי יהודה (step 29).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה holds a כהן גדול does not tear at all. שמואל holds the כהן גדול does tear, so he cannot simply be following רבי יהודה.

steps.title: שמואל agrees with רבי יהודה on one point only
steps.stepSummary: שמואל follows רבי יהודה on what counts as a real tear, but disagrees with him about whether a כהן גדול tears at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל agrees with רבי יהודה on one point and disagrees with him on the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. שמואל takes only one idea from רבי יהודה, not his whole view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל uses רבי יהודה's rule that a tear which leaves the edge whole is not a real tear. But unlike רבי יהודה, שמואל holds that a כהן גדול does tear in mourning. This lets the כהן גדול tear at the neck without breaking לא יפרם.

keyTerms.meaning: on one point
disagrees with him

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: the כהן גדול tears just below the neckline. That works because, following רבי יהודה, a tear that leaves the edge whole is not a 'real' tear. But שמואל rejects רבי יהודה's view that the כהן גדול never tears.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמוּאֵל סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּחֲדָא
phrases.english: Shmuel agrees with Rabbi Yehuda on one point
phrases.notes: That point is how to define a real tear, from step 29.

phrases.english: and disagrees with him on one point.
phrases.notes: That point is whether a כהן גדול tears at all. שמואל says he does.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּחֲדָא, וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 30 by limiting how far שמואל follows רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial agreement: one point accepted, one point rejected
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל follows רבי יהודה entirely, which would mean the כהן גדול never tears.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל accepts only רבי יהודה's definition of a real tear, and still holds the כהן גדול tears.

steps.title: New משנה: the more frequent and the holier come first
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins with two general rules of order: what is more frequent comes first, and what is holier comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Whatever is more frequent than another comes before it. And whatever is holier than another comes before it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new משנה about which comes first when two things happen together. This step gives the two general rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets two ways to decide what comes first. One is how often something happens (תדיר). The other is how holy it is (מקודש). The cases that follow are built on these rules.

keyTerms.meaning: short for מתניתין, our משנה
frequent, something that happens more often
holier, of greater holiness
comes first, takes priority

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of תדיר and מקודש comes up in many places in practical הלכה. For example, it decides which מצוה to do first when two come together.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Anything that is more frequent than another
comes before the other
and anything that is holier than another
comes before the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל הַתָּדִיר מֵחֲבֵירוֹ קוֹדֵם אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the tearing discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two things come together, the more frequent one comes first, and the holier one comes first.

steps.title: The anointed priest's bull comes before the community's bull
steps.stepSummary: If the bull of the כהן משיח and the bull of the community are both waiting, the כהן משיח's bull comes first in every part of its service.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the bull of the anointed כהן and the bull of the community are both waiting, the bull of the anointed כהן comes before the community's bull in all its steps.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies its rule of order to a specific case: two sin-offering bulls brought at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are פר קרבנות brought for a mistake. The משנה rules that the כהן משיח's bull is done first, and not just at the start, but at every stage of the service.

keyTerms.meaning: the bull brought by the anointed כהן גדול for his mistake
the bull brought for the community's mistake
are standing, waiting to be offered
in all its actions, every step of the service

phrases.english: If the bull of the anointed kohen and the bull of the community are waiting
the bull of the anointed kohen comes before the bull of the community
in all its actions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the general rules of step 32 to a specific pair of קרבנות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פר המשיח comes before the פר העדה in every step of its service.

steps.title: The גמרא asks for the source of 'more frequent comes first'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking where the משנה's rule that the more frequent thing comes first is learned from.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we learn these rules?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section begins. It asks for the source of the משנה's first rule, that whatever is more frequent comes first, and sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated the rule without giving a source. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches it, and the next step gives the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
From where are these things learned?
Frequent, something that happens often

phrases.english: Gemara:
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה whose rules were given in steps 32-33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the rule that the more frequent thing comes first.

steps.title: אביי learns it from the extra words 'daily burnt-offering'
steps.stepSummary: אביי points to a פסוק that says 'the morning burnt-offering' and then also 'the daily burnt-offering.' The extra words teach that whatever is frequent comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The פסוק says, 'Besides the burnt-offering of the morning, which is for a daily burnt-offering.' Since it already said 'burnt-offering of the morning,' why add 'daily burnt-offering'? The Torah is telling us: anything that is more frequent comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question with a פסוק about the extra holiday offerings. He shows that an extra phrase in the פסוק teaches the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'the morning burnt-offering' was already enough to know which offering is meant, so the word 'daily' (תמיד) seems extra. אביי says the Torah added it to give the reason the תמיד goes first: it is offered every day, so it is more frequent. From here we learn the general rule that whatever is more frequent comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: The morning burnt-offering
The daily burnt-offering, brought every day
Since already, a word that points out something extra in the פסוק
'The Merciful One,' meaning the Torah, or ה׳
Comes first, takes priority

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, 'תדיר קודם,' is used all over the תורה and in הלכה, for example when deciding which מצוה to do first.

phrases.english: Abaye said: As the verse states:
"Besides the burnt-offering of the morning,
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:23

phrases.english: which is for a daily burnt-offering."
(why do I need it?)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out these words in round brackets; the same question comes up again in a moment anyway.

phrases.english: Since it is already written "the burnt-offering of the morning,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'תמיד' in במדבר 28:23 teaches that the daily offering goes first because it is frequent, so whatever is more frequent comes first.

steps.title: The גמרא asks for the source of 'more holy comes first'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's second rule, that whoever is holier comes first, and asks where it is learned from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: Anyone who is holier than another comes before him. From where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the משנה's second rule and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the first rule has a source, the גמרא does the same for the second one. Here the rule is about people: the one with more holiness gets priority.

keyTerms.meaning: Holier, having more holiness
His fellow, the other one
From where do we learn this?

phrases.english: And anyone who is more sanctified than another
precedes that other one.
From where do we derive this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הַמְקוּדָּשׁ מֵחֲבֵירוֹ הוּא קוֹדֵם אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ. מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finding the source of the first rule in step 35, the גמרא turns to the second rule of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the rule that whoever is holier comes first.

steps.title: School of רבי ישמעאל: 'And you shall sanctify him' gives the כהן priority
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns from 'וקדשתו' that a כהן gets priority in every holy matter: opening first, blessing first, and taking the best portion first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And you shall sanctify him' means in every matter of holiness: he opens first, he blesses first, and he takes a nice portion first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a teaching that the Torah tells us to honor the כהן and give him priority because he is holy. It lists three examples of that priority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'וקדשתו' is about a כהן, and it commands us to treat him as holy. The school of רבי ישמעאל explains this as giving him the first turn in anything connected to holiness. This shows the general rule: the one with more holiness goes first.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall sanctify him,' said about a כהן
The school (students) of רבי ישמעאל
A matter of holiness
A nice, choice portion

steps.whatToRemember: Both rules of the משנה now have sources: 'more frequent comes first' comes from the extra word תמיד, and 'more holy comes first' comes from וקדשתו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice that a כהן is called first to the Torah and is given honor in leading blessings.

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"And you shall sanctify him"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:8, a פסוק about a כהן.

phrases.english: with regard to any matter of holiness:

phrases.english: and to bless first,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'וקדשתו' teaches that the holier person, the כהן, gets priority in every matter of holiness.
